title: The generic ordinary component count is a lower bound after shrinking
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Suppose the scheme-theoretic generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has exactly $n$ irreducible components, where $n\geq0$ is a finite integer. There is a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that $X_t$ has at least $n$ irreducible components for every $t\in V$. These are ordinary irreducible components over $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field], without passage to a field extension. No flatness, separatedness or Noetherian assumption on $f$ or $Y$ is imposed.

proof.text: If $n=0$, take $V=Y$; it is nonempty since $\eta\in Y$, and the lower bound is automatic. For $n>0$ set $I=\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ and enumerate the distinct components of $X_\eta$ as $(C_i)_{i\in I}$. By [def-weil-irreducible-components] they are nonempty closed irreducible subsets, and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] says they cover $X_\eta$.

For the remaining steps assume $n>0$. Write $p_t:X_t\to X$ for each canonical fibre projection. Apply [lem-trf-closed-generic-subset-finite-type-model] to the given finite type $f$ with $y=\eta$ and the closed subset $A=C_i$ of Step 1. For each $i\in I$ obtain a reduced scheme $Z_i$, a closed immersion $j_i:Z_i\hookrightarrow X$ with image $D_i=\overline{p_\eta(C_i)}$, and finite type $h_i=f\circ j_i$. Put $D_{i,t}=p_t^{-1}(D_i)$. The lemma supplies a homeomorphism from $|(Z_i)_t|$ onto this closed subspace of $|X_t|$, induced by the canonical fibre map, and gives $D_{i,\eta}=C_i$. Thus the family supplied to Step 3 has exactly the prescribed generic traces and the required finite-type composites; the supports are subsets of the original fibre $X_t$, rather than of a scalar extension.

For $i\ne j$, an inclusion $C_i\subseteq C_j$ would contradict distinctness: $C_j$ is irreducible and maximality of $C_i$ forces $C_i=C_j$ by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Apply [lem-trf-generic-closed-pieces-simultaneous-spread] to the given finite type $f:X\to Y$, with $Y$ irreducible and $\eta$ its generic point, the finite index set $I=\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ from Step 1, and the closed immersions of Step 2. Step 2 supplies closedness of every $D_{i,t}$ and finite type of each composite with $f$; their generic supports are exactly the nonempty irreducible $C_i$, which cover by Step 1 and are incomparable as just shown. Obtain an open $V$ containing $\eta$, hence nonempty, on which the $D_{i,t}$ are nonempty closed covering pieces and every $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$, $i\ne j$, is dense in $D_{i,t}$.

proof.text: Fix $t\in V$. Apply [lem-trf-closed-cover-dense-complements-component-injection] to $T=|X_t|$, $I=\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ and $E_i=D_{i,t}$: Step 3 supplies the nonempty closed covering pieces and dense relative complements. Obtain pairwise distinct components $K_i$ of $T$. By [def-weil-irreducible-components], these are ordinary components of $X_t$. Thus $i\mapsto (K_i,\ K_i\text{ is a component of }X_t)$ defines an injection $\operatorname{Fin}(n)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Irr}(X_t)$, where $\operatorname{Irr}(X_t)$ denotes the set of ordinary irreducible components. This is precisely the asserted lower bound. The same open $V$ works for every $t$; only this finite selection of components depends on $t$. No field extension or irreducibility of a specialized piece is needed.
